title: Reliability Ops Hackweek: Sprint Plan + Postmortem Probes
body:
Purpose:
This is a working plan for an 1-week cross-functional hackweek focused on pragmatic reliability improvements tied directly to measurable SLO outcomes and a short set of postmortem "probes" we will run against low-risk production slices. Goal: shrink p99 latency by 15% for small-text generation paths and reduce sustained error-budget burn rate for the embeddings route by 30% over the next 90 days via targeted experiments and fast followup runbooks.

Context / why now:
- Recent spikes in error budget consumption during regional deploys (see JIRA:SRE-3421).
- Multiple teams report increased tail latency when model sequence length >512.
- Opportunity window: hackweek paired with canary window for Dedicated can take low-risk traffic slices.

Scope (what we will do this week):
1) Measurement sprint (Mon-Tue)
   - Audit existing instrumentation (trace spans, histogram buckets). Owner: Mei Lin.
   - Add an 8ms bucket to the token-path histograms; validate in staging. (PR: serving-runtime#1187)
   - Build quick dashboard: p50/p95/p99 for: text-gen-small, text-gen-medium, embeddings.

2) Targeted experiments (Wed-Thu)
   - KV cache prefix retention tweaks: experiment with TTL=60s vs 300s on high reuse keys. Hypothesis: smaller TTL reduces memory contention, improves p99. Owner: Diego Ramos.
   - Dynamic batching policy variant: reduce max-batch-size from 64->48 for short sequences to lower head-of-line blocking. Owner: Liam O'Connor.
   - Fast-quantization fallback test on non-critical model variant to measure latency/cost tradeoffs. Owner: Priya Shah.

3) Postmortem probes (Fri)
   - Run controlled error injection (non-cascading) on a 0.5% traffic slice to validate guardrail behavior and incident playbooks.
   - Execute alerting fire-drill: trigger a synthetic p99 breach and practice on-call runbook steps, communication cadence, and incident handoff.

Success criteria (end of hackweek):
- Dashboards reflect new instrumentation and reliably show p99 at aggregate and by-region granularity.
- At least two experiments have before/after metrics recorded and linked artifacts (PRs and dashboards).
- Runbook updates merged to Confluence and playbook quick-links added to the on-call Slack workflow.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: experiment causes elevated error budget burn. Mitigation: start on 0.1% traffic, automatic rollback on >3x baseline error rate.
- Risk: untested metric buckets create noisy dashboards. Mitigation: validate buckets in staging and tag new metrics with "hackweek-temp" label.

Short timeline / milestones:
- Fri prior to hackweek: finalize experiment design + acceptances (owners + SRE lead).
- Day 1 (Mon): instrumentation audit complete; dashboard skeleton up.
- Day 2 (Tue): metric buckets live in staging; change approvals queued.
- Day 3-4 (Wed-Thu): run experiments on limited traffic slices; collect 6-12 hours of stable signals.
- Day 5 (Fri): postmortem probes + fire drill; triage learnings; merge immediate runbook fixes.

Who does what (working RACI-lite):
- Aisha Patel (owner): overall program lead, coordination with product and infra, final go/no-go.
- Mei Lin (metrics): instrumentation updates, dashboard lead.
- Diego Ramos (runtime experiments): KV cache, memory profiling.
- Liam O'Connor (batching): batching policy variants, testing harness.
- Priya Shah (model variants): quantization fallback test and validation.
- Eng-Console pair (oncall): ensure rollback automation and Slack integration.

Measurement plan (what to capture):
- p99 latency per route, per-region, with 1-minute resolution histograms.
- Error rate (5xx + model-runtime errors) and error budget burn over 1h/6h/24h windows.
- Cost per 1000 tokens for the quantization variant.
- Observability: traces that correlate request size -> batch size -> latency.

Post-hackweek followups (30/60/90 day):
- 30d: stabilize experiment winners behind a feature flag for larger canary (10% traffic). Product/infra review.
- 60d: if stable, convert to rollout plan and infra config change + cost impact report.
- 90d: adopt as default or rollback and document learnings in reliability knowledge base.

Open questions / notes to self (informal):
- Can we route only internal-traffic tokens through quantized variant to reduce user-visible risk?
- Should we add a short-lived Prometheus job to backfill histograms for the last 7d? (Mei to investigate)
- Need runbook snippet for "batching policy flip" that includes exact CLI commands for rollback.

Meeting & communication plan:
- Kickoff: Mon 09:15 SRE-ops room (30m) — align owners and validate test windows.
- Daily sync: 30m standup Mon-Fri 16:30 — quick blockers and measurement review.
- Friday wrap: 60m retro + merged PR checklist; publish summary to #sre-reliability and link Confluence page.

Artifacts to produce this week (minimal):
- Quick dashboard (Grafana link) + template screenshot for playbook.
- 2 short PRs (instrumentation + runtime tweak).
- Oncall runbook edits in Confluence.
- Short postmortem note capturing outcomes and next steps.

Appendix: quick experiment definitions (copyable):
- KV-TTL-LOW: set KV_TTL_SECONDS=60 for pipeline "prefix-4"; sample rate 1% -> 0.1% -> 1% traffic ramp. Rollback: unset and redeploy.
- BATCH-SZ-SMALLSEQ: override MAX_BATCH=48 for route: text-gen-small; monitor p50/p99 and CPU utilization.
- QUANT-FALLBACK: deploy quantized variant behind header X-Quant-Test:1 for internal traffic only; measure token latency & perplexity delta.

---
Notes: this doc is intentionally lightweight and action-oriented. Keep experiment definitions terse; capture full analysis in the postmortem note with graphs and precise numbers.
